description:
Blind-spot `2026-05-04-004045` documented an asymmetry between
`benchbox/core/primitives/catalog/loader.py:_parse_validation_queries`
(forwards 7 fields: id/sql/expected_rows/expected_rows_min/
expected_rows_max/expected_values/check_expression) and the
write_primitives-local equivalent (which forwards
`expected_value_min`, `expected_value_max`, and validation-level
`platform_overrides` in addition).

The shared loader is consumed by `transaction_primitives` today. Any
future agent reaching for `load_operations_catalog` in another
benchmark area silently gets the older, narrower validation_query
shape -- the field is just dropped, no error.

Sweep verification (2026-05-05): operation-level `platform_overrides`
IS present in the shared loader, but validation-query-level
`expected_value_min`, `expected_value_max`, and `platform_overrides`
are NOT.

anti_patterns.dont: delete the write_primitives-local loader as a side-effect
anti_patterns.why: if the chosen path is (a) incremental extension, leave the local loader in place and let it inherit from the shared one explicitly.

anti_patterns.dont: introduce a third copy of the validation-query parsing logic. If (b) is chosen, the write_primitives loader becomes a thin call into the shared one, not a parallel implementation.

preserves.behavior: ValidationQuery dataclass shape is backwards-compatible (new params are optional with sensible defaults).
transaction_primitives validation behaviour is unchanged for catalogs that don't use the new fields.
write_primitives validation_query parsing continues to accept all three currently-supported extensions (`expected_value_min`, `expected_value_max`, `platform_overrides`).

verifications.description: Shared loader forwards the three previously-missing fields
Cross-loader parity test exists and passes

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/core/transaction_primitives/ -m fast -q
verifications.description: transaction_primitives still loads its catalog cleanly

work_units.notes:
Two paths:
(a) extend `benchbox/core/primitives/catalog/loader.py`
    `_parse_validation_queries` to forward the three missing
    fields, leave the write_primitives-local loader as a thin
    wrapper.
(b) delete the write_primitives-local loader and have
    `load_write_primitives_catalog` delegate to
    `load_operations_catalog` end-to-end.
Path (a) is incremental and safer; path (b) eliminates the
duplication root cause. Pick one based on how much
write_primitives-local logic is unique vs. just-different.
work_units.summary: Decide: extend shared loader, or fold write_primitives-local into shared

work_units.notes:
Port `_parse_validation_platform_overrides` and
`_parse_expected_value_bounds` from the write_primitives loader
into the shared loader (or its helpers). Build the new
ValidationQuery via `build_validation_query(...)` so callers
that don't pass the new fields keep working.
work_units.summary: Implement chosen path; ensure both validation_query parsers expose identical shapes

work_units.notes:
Smallest viable: a fast-marked unit test that introspects both
loader functions' kwargs to `build_validation_query(...)` and
asserts the field set is identical. Larger: a structural diff
between the two loader files for the validation-query block.
work_units.summary: Add a CI grep/test that fails when one loader gains a validation_query field the other does not
